name: Venezuela
system_note: Formally a presidential republic; the PSUV still controls state institutions.
snapshot: A US raid in January seized Nicolás Maduro and flew him to New York, but his vice president took over and Washington chose to deal with her rather than the opposition.
culture: Venezuela holds the world's largest proven oil reserves, which shaped everything from its 20th-century boom to its collapse. Baseball is the national sport, and the Venezuelan team won the 2026 World Baseball Classic. Joropo music, played with harp and cuatro, and arepas are national staples. Its beauty pageant winners are national celebrities.
society: Under Hugo Chávez and Maduro, oil revenue funded social programmes until mismanagement and US sanctions caused one of the worst economic collapses outside wartime. Nearly eight million people, a quarter of the population, have left. Hyperinflation peaked in 2018. Opposition leader María Corina Machado won the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize.

story: For more than a decade Venezuela's opposition, backed by Washington, tried to remove Nicolás Maduro through elections, protests and sanctions, as some 8 million people fled the country. In January the US finally removed him, by force. What followed surprised almost everyone: Washington chose to work not with the opposition but with Maduro's own vice president.

After the 3 January raid, a court installed Delcy Rodríguez as acting president, and the Trump administration recognised her as head of state, lifted sanctions on her personally on 1 April, then on the central bank, and sent officials to Caracas to discuss access to Venezuela's oil and minerals (AP via Herald Extra). Maduro has pleaded not guilty in New York and legally remains president. In March, Venezuela even beat the US to win the World Baseball Classic, and Rodríguez posed with the trophy at the presidential palace. Opposition leader María Corina Machado, the 2025 Nobel Peace laureate, held rallies abroad as her movement was sidelined. On 23 September, in her first UN General Assembly speech, Rodríguez promised that "elections will be held in Venezuela," but at the "right moment" decided by Venezuelans, with no date; she met Trump the night before (NPR via KAXE). Venezuela changed hands without changing regimes.
briefing.power: Formally a presidential republic; in practice the ruling PSUV controls all institutions. Rodríguez governs as acting president under a court order, with the National Assembly led by her brother Jorge. The military remains a central power broker.
briefing.holders: Acting President Delcy Rodríguez (PSUV), since January 2026.
